title: The battle inside
hook: the fiercest fight in the Granth is with the five thieves in your own mind

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Nihang orders, and your line, the old ways kept. A week of swords, flags and horsemen. Today, the last day of sword and saint, and the fight the Guru Granth Sahib cares about most. Day two hundred eighty-one.

You've had a day where nobody attacked you and you still lost. You snapped at someone you love. You scrolled for an hour you didn't have. You wanted the bigger slice, the last word, the credit. No enemy crossed the wall. The trouble started inside the house. For a week we've talked about swords. But if you open the Guru Granth Sahib looking for battles, you'll find very few with armies in them. The fiercest fight in the Granth happens somewhere else. Today: the battle inside.
screen: `NOBODY ATTACKED, AND YOU STILL LOST.` → `A WEEK OF SWORDS.` → `THE FIERCEST FIGHT IS ELSEWHERE.`

segments.voice: The Granth names the enemy many times, and it has five faces. Sikhs call them the five thieves. Kaam, lust, desire that grabs. Krodh, anger. Lobh, greed. Moh, attachment, clinging to what we can't keep. And ahankar, pride, the ego that makes everything about me. We've met them before on this path. One hymn of Guru Amar Das pictures it plainly: inside this body live five thieves, and they plunder the nectar within. Not out there. In here. Now listen to Guru Nanak, in the Japji, the morning prayer. One short line in the twenty-eighth verse, man jeetai jag jeet. Conquer your own mind, and you've conquered the world. Think about what that does to everything we learned this week. The saint-soldier's courage. The kirpan, mercy first. Every other means first. Fair, even in conflict. The calm face in gatka. Every one of those depends on winning an inner fight first: against anger that wants to strike, pride that wants to win, fear that wants to run. A soldier who hasn't fought the five thieves isn't a saint-soldier, just a soldier. The Granth's weapons for this fight aren't made of steel. The Name, remembered. The company of good people, the sangat. The Guru's word. Honest work and sharing. And humility, the opposite of ahankar. Sikhs don't expect to win it once and for all. It's a daily fight, and most days the wins are small: one sharp word not said, one craving let pass. That's the battle the whole week pointed to.
screen: `FIVE THIEVES — LUST, ANGER, GREED.` · `ATTACHMENT, AND PRIDE.` · `CONQUER THE MIND, CONQUER THE WORLD.` · `THE WEAPONS: NAME, SANGAT, HUMILITY.` · then, large: `THE REAL BATTLE.`

segments.voice: Sit comfortably, and look inside for a moment, the way a guard walks the walls at night. Which of the five is loudest in you today? Anger, greed, desire, clinging, or pride? Don't fight it yet. Just name it, quietly, the way you'd name a visitor. Then choose one small win against it for later today. One word you won't say, or one thing you'll let go of. Rest with the breath. The bell holds the time.
The battle inside. The Granth's fiercest fight is with the five thieves in your own mind. Conquer the mind, and you conquer the world.
Your line: the real battle. Today, win one small inner fight: the word unsaid or the thing let go. Day two hundred eighty-one.

howItsDone: Sikhs speak of the five thieves (kaam, krodh, lobh, moh, ahankar) as the real enemies, and fight them through naam simran, the sangat, the Guru's word, honest work and humility.

fork.setup: you're a saint-soldier. what fight comes first?
options: the one against the nearest enemy army.
the one against anger, greed and pride in your own mind.
the one you're most likely to win.
fork.reveal: the Granth's fiercest fight is inside. without it the soldier is only a soldier.

original.note: Gurmukhi, from the Japji, verse 28: conquer the mind, and you conquer the world.

trapdoor: what you thought: Sikhism is a warrior religion.
what it means: the fiercest fight in the Granth is with the five thieves in your own mind.
what a scholar hears: kaam, krodh, lobh, moh and ahankar recur throughout the Granth as the panj chor; Japji 28 (Ang 6) makes conquest of the mind the conquest of the world.

sources.ref: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 600 (Sorath, Guru Amar Das): five thieves within the body

notes: The Gurmukhi line from Japji 28 is given in the original only; the English is a paraphrase. Confirm spelling and transliteration.

The 'five thieves in the body' image (they plunder the amrit within) is attributed to Guru Amar Das, Sorath, Ang 600; the English is a paraphrase, not a translation. Reviewer changed 'stealing the jewel of the Name' to 'plunder the nectar within' to track the original more closely. Confirm the Ang, attribution and wording.
